clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant; heterozygous HNRNPDL variants (classically affecting a conserved residue in the second RNA-recognition motif) impair the function of an RNA-binding protein with a prion-like low-complexity domain.
Presents as adult-onset proximal limb-girdle weakness.
A distinctive tendency to limitation of finger and toe flexion was described in the original families.
Cataracts have been reported in a proportion of affected individuals.
Creatine kinase is mildly to moderately elevated.
Muscle biopsy shows dystrophic change with rimmed vacuoles.
First delineated in Brazilian and Uruguayan kindreds.
reference.pathophysiology: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy D3 is an autosomal dominant subtype caused by heterozygous variants in HNRNPDL on chromosome 4q21, which encodes heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein D-like, an RNA-binding protein that shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm and regulates transcription, alternative splicing and messenger-RNA metabolism. Nearly all reported families carry variants affecting a conserved residue within the second RNA-recognition motif, and because the protein contains a prion-like low-complexity domain, the mechanism is thought to involve disturbed RNA processing together with aberrant protein aggregation, akin to other RNA-binding-protein myopathies. First delineated in Brazilian and Uruguayan kindreds, the phenotype is an adult-onset proximal limb-girdle weakness with a distinctive tendency to limitation of finger and toe flexion, and cataracts have been reported in some affected individuals. Muscle biopsy shows dystrophic change with rimmed vacuoles.
additionalDifferentials: Other RNA-binding-protein myopathies (for example hnRNPA1 and hnRNPA2B1)
additionalInvestigations: Next-generation sequencing gene panel or whole-exome sequencing including HNRNPDL
Muscle biopsy (dystrophic change with rimmed vacuoles)
reference.prognosis: Progression is slow and many patients retain ambulation for years. Cataracts, when present, may require ophthalmic management.
pitfalls: The combination of cataracts and weakness may be misattributed to myotonic dystrophy.
Rimmed vacuoles may falsely suggest sporadic inclusion body myositis.
Rarity and ancestry-specific reporting can delay recognition.
Variable expressivity within families may obscure the dominant inheritance pattern.
references: Consensus classification of the limb-girdle muscular dystrophies
management: Recognise there is no disease-specific drug therapy and use physiotherapy and occupational therapy to preserve proximal strength and address limitation of finger and toe flexion
Arrange ophthalmological review and cataract surgery where cataracts develop
Provide respiratory monitoring with ventilatory support as required
Deliver multidisciplinary neuromuscular rehabilitation, with ambulation often retained for years
Provide genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance and family screening
Arrange specialist neuromuscular follow-up for diagnosis and surveillance
